# MaterialCraft — Procedural Material Designer

Studio: Creative. Source: https://github.com/PiJellyPin/MaterialCraft.

Create procedural materials with MaterialCraft node graphs. Preserve the editable graph and all source textures and meshes; exported maps are companions to the master. Inspect material channels and report unsupported nodes or interchange limits. Do not claim compatibility with proprietary Substance projects or an unverified browser/library handoff. Work only in the assigned project and task working folder. Use studio-mcp for authorized library access. Report a library save only after its confirmed immutable revision; preserve the expected base revision and stop on conflicts.

MaterialCraft 0.5.0 uses editable `.sbs` XML packages. Keep linked SBS packages and source images at their exact relative paths. Browser editing uses the genuine material graph, parameter panels and CPU renderer; its existing Save/Ctrl+S, Save As/Shift+Ctrl+S and File > Save a Copy actions require a confirmed immutable library revision. Copy preserves the original asset binding. An unconfirmed save must be reconciled before another snapshot; retain later edits and use Save As after a known revision conflict.

For native work, call `studio_run_native` with `appId: "materialcraft"` and argv. The installed executable is `/usr/local/bin/materialcraft`. Start with `["--help"]`. Its `exec` commands take an explicit `--root` under the assigned task, `--graph` for the native SBS input, and an explicit output path after `--save`; omitting that value can consume the next command as a filename. Use `graph.inspect` with `compact=true` to inspect nodes and parameters; there is no `node.inspect` command.

A new empty graph uses `["exec", "--root", "<working-folder>", "--save", "<working-folder>/Untitled material.sbs", "graph.new", "size=512", "name=Graph"]`. For continuation, open the exact assigned input with `studio_open_input`, then run `exec --root <working-folder> --graph <master.sbs> --save <continued.sbs> graph.set size=256`, or change an existing node through `node.set node=<id> params.<name>=<value>`. Reopen the saved graph and render the affected material channel to verify the result. Exports supplement the editable master.

Use `studio_save_input_revision` for the exact input asset, or `studio_save_native_project` for a new native package. The packager follows explicit relative SBS dependencies and resource paths, including nested packages; it preserves the original XML and linked bytes, and never scans unrelated files. File > Open in the browser accepts the native SBS with its selected linked files. Missing, escaping or unsupported inputs must be reported, never replaced with invented data. Native and browser support for proprietary Substance nodes is partial; preserve the master and disclose unsupported features.
